scope: gene-rule corrections for the OR-rule reactions that are essential in at least one carbon-source condition where the wild-type model grows (scripts/essential_or_rules.py: 55 in B. thetaiotaomicron, 85 in P. putida, 47 in S. oneidensis, 70 in S. meliloti), beyond those already in v0.2. Same rules as v0.2, adjudicated from RefSeq product names and enzymology only: R1 remove genes annotated as a different enzyme, a family/domain, or a non-enzyme (regulators, ribosomal proteins, thioredoxins as substrates, hypotheticals); R2 join annotated subunits with AND; R3 leave same-name paralogs, generic names ('aminotransferase', 'aldolase') and same-family members with no specific alternative; R5 (new) a diffusion or porin reaction keeps only porins, and a rule whose every gene is a different enzyme becomes empty (the reaction then carries no gene, i.e. it can no longer be knocked out) rather than keeping a wrong assignment. ABC-transporter and PTS rules were skipped (complexes lumped across systems). VERIFIER OUTCOME (5 Sept 2026): applied on top of v0.1+v0.2, the full set changed 391 gene-condition predictions to essential of which only 21 were experimentally important, so patches whose changes the fitness data contradict are marked status='held' with the reason; the runner applies only status='accepted' patches. The held reasons fall into three classes: transporter gaps for vitamins that the media contain, reaction-level essentiality artefacts unmasked by removing a false isozyme, and adjudications the data show to be wrong. UPDATE (5 Sept 2026, later): four held patches were re-adjudicated — the B. thetaiotaomicron pyruvate-carboxylase rule is accepted together with a Btheta-scoped PPCK direction patch (universe_patches_v0.1.json), and the three riboflavin-synthase rules held as transporter gaps or unexplained were re-adjudicated under R4 (a second annotated isozyme present in the genome: PP_0515, SMc01777, SO3468) — 24 remain held. UPDATE (5 Sept 2026, cycle 4): the 24 held patches were re-tested one at a time on top of medium completion and the model patches (scripts/evaluate_held_rules.py, results/carbon_fitness_multi/held_rules_reevaluation.tsv): 11 are now accepted (neutral, or resolved by an R4 isozyme, an R5 empty rule, the thiamine-uptake model patch, or the glycolaldehyde by-product sink; PMPK on the annotation with the verifier's mixed result recorded), 3 are rejected (the annotation adjudication was wrong and the original rule stands: AGPR, HISTP, PHETA1) and 10 remain held (one biomass-template question, the folate-branch dephosphorylation, one unannotated isozyme, and seven single-condition contradictions).
